description: The EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation, directly applicable across all Member States, replacing AMLD4/5 customer-facing provisions.
6th Anti-Money Laundering Directive — institutional and supervisory framework to be implemented by Member States.
New EU supervisory authority established by Regulation (EU) 2024/1620. Becomes operational 2025, takes over direct supervision of highest-risk entities 2028.
Issues binding technical standards and guidelines on AML/CFT. Transfers supervisory convergence role to AMLA from 2025.
International standard-setter for AML/CFT. AMLR requirements aligned with FATF Recommendations 2012 (as updated).
Obliged entities must apply CDD measures when establishing a business relationship, carrying out occasional transactions ≥€10,000, or when suspicion of ML/TF arises.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 20: "obliged entities shall apply CDD measures"

description: Mandatory EDD for high-risk third countries, PEPs, and complex/unusual transactions. Includes enhanced monitoring and senior management approval.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 34: mandatory for listed triggers (HRTCs, PEPs, unusual transactions)

description: Proportionate measures permitted for lower-risk situations. Cannot be applied to PEPs, high-risk third countries, or when ML/TF suspicion exists.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 31: "obliged entities may apply simplified due diligence" in lower-risk situations

description: Obliged entities must identify and verify the beneficial owner of legal entities as part of CDD (Art. 22 AMLR). 25% or more ownership or control threshold for companies. No percentage threshold applies to trusts/foundations — all persons in the trust structure must be identified.

metadata.note: 25% threshold applies to legal entities only; no threshold for trusts/foundations
metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 22: "obliged entities shall identify and take reasonable measures to verify the identity of the beneficial owner"

description: Politically Exposed Persons: enhanced scrutiny, senior management approval, source of wealth/funds verification. Former PEPs must be treated as PEPs for an appropriate risk-based period after ceasing public function (Art. 45(4) AMLR — no fixed duration mandated; risk-sensitive assessment required).

metadata.cessation_note: Risk-based period per Art. 45(4) — no fixed duration mandated by AMLR
metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 44: mandatory enhanced scrutiny — no discretion once PEP status confirmed

description: Obliged entities must promptly report suspicions of ML/TF to FIUs. Tipping-off prohibition applies. Attempted transactions must also be reported.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 69: "obliged entities shall promptly report" — absolute obligation

description: Obliged entities must implement a risk-based approach informed by supranational (SNRA), national (NRA), and entity-level risk assessments. Proportionate to identified risks.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 8: "obliged entities shall take appropriate steps to identify, assess and understand the risks"

description: Written BWRA required covering all products, services, customers, geographies. Must be updated at least annually and upon material changes.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 10: written BWRA is mandatory

description: Obliged entities must ensure staff receive regular training on AML/CFT obligations, relevant typologies, and internal policies. Must be role-specific.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 18: "obliged entities shall take measures to ensure that their employees are aware of the provisions"

description: Must appoint a senior compliance officer at management body level (AML Officer) and a dedicated MLRO. Both must have adequate seniority, resources, and access.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 11: appointment of compliance officer and MLRO is mandatory

description: CDD records and transaction data must be retained for 5 years from end of business relationship or transaction date. Extendable to 10 years by national law.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 77: "obliged entities shall retain" CDD and transaction records

description: Payment service providers must accompany transfers with complete payer/payee information. Aligned with FATF Recommendation 16 and TFR Regulation.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 83: mandatory — payment service providers shall ensure information accompanies transfers

canonical_name: Internal Controls & Compliance Programme — Art. 17 AMLR
description: Obliged entities must establish written policies, controls, and procedures. Must be approved by senior management and communicated to all relevant staff.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 17: written internal controls programme is mandatory

description: Entities subject to AMLR obligations: credit institutions, financial institutions, crypto-asset service providers (CASPs), auditors, lawyers, notaries, tax advisors, real estate agents, trust/company service providers, and others.
Conversion, transfer, concealment, disguising, acquisition, possession or use of criminal proceeds, knowing that property is derived from criminal activity.
Provision or collection of funds with the intention or knowledge that they will be used for terrorist activities.
Individuals entrusted with prominent public functions including Heads of State, senior politicians, judicial officials, central bank governors, ambassadors, board members of state-owned enterprises.

Natural person(s) who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement. For legal entities: 25% or more ownership or control threshold. For trusts and similar arrangements: NO percentage threshold — settlor, all trustees, protector, all beneficiaries, and any person exercising effective control must be identified.

metadata.threshold_pct_trusts: N/A — all natural persons in the structure

description: Countries with strategic deficiencies in AML/CFT frameworks as identified by the EU Commission under delegated regulation. Triggers mandatory EDD.
Persons providing crypto-asset services as defined in MiCAR. CASPs are obliged entities under AMLR from its application date. Subject to full CDD and SAR obligations.
National authority receiving and analysing SARs. FIUs in each Member State. FIU.net coordinates cross-border intelligence sharing in the EU.
Commission-level assessment of ML/TF risks affecting the EU internal market. Published every 2 years. Must inform entity-level BWRA.
Member State assessment of ML/TF risks in their jurisdiction. Must be published and communicated to obliged entities. Must inform entity-level BWRA.

metadata.source_quote: Directive (EU) 2024/1640 Art. 8: "Each Member State shall carry out a national risk assessment to identify, assess, understand and mitigate the risks of money laundering and terrorist financing, and the risks of non-implementation and evasion of targeted financial sanctions affecting it."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amld6-2024.txt

description: AMLR restricts acceptance of cash payments above €10,000 for goods/services by professionals (Art. 80). Some Member States may set lower limits.

canonical_name: Wire Transfer / Crypto Transfer Information Requirements
description: Payment service providers must accompany wire transfers with full payer/payee data (AMLR Art. 83 / TFR Regulation (EU) 2023/1113). For crypto-asset transfers: full originator/beneficiary information is required at any amount — there is NO minimum threshold (TFR2 Art. 4). The €1,000 threshold applies only to wire transfers without payment service providers.

metadata.note: Crypto transfers: no minimum threshold per TFR2 (Regulation 2023/1113)

description: Casinos must verify customer identity for transactions ≥€2,000 (purchase/exchange of chips, etc.).
AMLR applies from 10 July 2027 (3 years after OJ publication). CASPs have transitional provisions. Certain obligations may be earlier via AMLA RTS.
Member States must transpose AMLD6 into national law by 10 July 2026, one year before AMLR application.
AMLA takes over direct supervision of highest-risk credit institutions and CASPs across the EU from January 2028.
AMLA will develop binding Regulatory Technical Standards on CDD procedures, including enhanced due diligence for high-risk third countries and PEPs.
Regulation (EU) 2023/1114. CASPs licensed under MiCAR are obliged entities under AMLR. Licensing authority coordinates with AML supervisors.
Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. Applies to financial entities including credit institutions and investment firms. Relevant to AML system resilience requirements.
Regulation (EU) 2016/679. AML data processing must comply with GDPR. Art. 77 AMLR data retention obligations must be balanced against GDPR erasure rights.
Banks and other credit institutions are primary obliged entities under AMLR. Subject to the full set of CDD, SAR, and internal controls obligations.
Investment firms regulated under MiFID II are obliged entities under AMLR. CDD applies to all clients and transactions.
Life insurance and intermediaries dealing with investment-linked products are obliged entities. Beneficiary screening required.

Obliged entities may rely on third parties to conduct CDD, but remain fully liable for compliance failures. Third party must be an obliged entity itself, subject to equivalent AML/CFT requirements. Immediate availability of CDD data required.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 28: reliance on third parties is permitted but not required — discretionary

description: Parent undertakings must implement group-wide AML/CFT policies and procedures. Subsidiaries in third countries must apply group standards where local law permits; where it does not, parent must notify home state supervisor.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 15: parent undertakings shall implement group-wide policies
metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 16: "To this end, a parent undertaking shall perform a group-wide risk assessment, taking into account the business-wide risk assessment performed by all branches and subsidiaries of the group, and establish and implement group-wide policies, procedures and controls, including on data protection and on information sharing within the group for AML/CFT purposes and to ensure that employees within the group are aware of the requirements arising from this Regulation."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

description: Credit institutions must conduct enhanced CDD on correspondent relationships. Must assess respondent's AML/CFT controls, obtain senior management approval, document respective responsibilities. Shell bank prohibition maintained.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 38: enhanced CDD on correspondent relationships is mandatory

canonical_name: PEP Family Members and Close Associates
description: Family members (spouse/partner, children and their spouses, parents) and known close associates of PEPs are subject to equivalent enhanced scrutiny under AMLR Art. 44. Enhanced measures continue for an appropriate risk-based period after the PEP ceases their public function — no fixed duration is mandated.

canonical_name: Prohibition on Anonymous Accounts — Art. 79 AMLR
description: Credit institutions and financial institutions must not keep anonymous accounts, passbooks, or safe-deposit boxes. Existing anonymous accounts must be subject to CDD measures and identified before any transaction.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 79: prohibition — no discretion

description: A credit institution incorporated in a jurisdiction where it has no physical presence and which is not affiliated with a regulated financial group. AMLR prohibits correspondent relationships with shell banks.

Obliged entities must monitor business relationships on an ongoing basis, including scrutiny of transactions to ensure consistency with knowledge of customer, business profile, and risk. CDD documents must be kept up to date.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 25: "obliged entities shall monitor the business relationship on an ongoing basis"

canonical_name: Customer Identification and Verification — Art. 21 AMLR
description: Obliged entities must identify and verify customer identity using reliable, independent source documents. For legal entities: identification of legal form, registered address, directors, and beneficial owners.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 21: identification and verification is mandatory

description: Trusts and similar legal arrangements are subject to AMLR BO disclosure. Trustees must identify themselves as trustees. BO = settlor, trustees, protector, beneficiaries, and any natural person exercising effective control.

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 1 — Subject Matter and Scope
description: Establishes that AMLR lays down rules on prevention of the use of the financial system for ML/TF purposes. Directly applicable in all Member States without transposition. Covers obliged entities' internal procedures, CDD, reporting, and group compliance.

Provides comprehensive definitions for all terms used in AMLR including: obliged entity, business relationship, beneficial owner, PEP, FIU, credit institution, financial institution, occasional transaction, and others. The primary definitional source for the entire AMLR framework.

metadata.note: Primary definitional article — defines all key terms referenced throughout AMLR

description: Lists all persons subject to AMLR obligations: credit institutions, financial institutions, CASPs, auditors, external accountants, tax advisors, notaries, lawyers (in specific circumstances), real estate agents and developers, trust/company service providers, high-value goods dealers, and gambling service providers.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Designates who is subject to AMLR — non-discretionary

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 6 — Exemptions for Certain Financial Activities
description: Member States may exempt natural or legal persons that carry out financial activity on an occasional or very limited basis from AMLR obligations, where strict low-risk criteria are met. Exemptions must be notified to the Commission.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 4: Member States MAY exempt limited-activity persons
metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 6: "With the exception of persons engaged in the activity of money remittance as defined in Article 4, point (22), of Directive (EU) 2015/2366, Member States may decide to exempt legal or natural persons that engage in a financial activity as listed in Annex I, points (2) to (12), (14) and (15), to Directive 2013/36/EU on an occasional or very limited basis where there is little risk of money laundering or terrorist financing from the requirements set out in this Regulation, provided that all of the following criteria are met: (a) the financial activity is limited in absolute terms; (b) the financial activity is limited on a transaction basis; (c) the financial activity is not the main activity of such persons; (d) the financial activity is ancillary and directly related to the main activity of such persons; (e) the main activity of such persons is not an activity referred to in Article 3, point (3)(a) to (d) or (g) of this Regulation; (f) the financial activity is provided only to the customers of the main activity of such persons and is not generally offered to the public."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

description: The Commission may determine that certain third countries have equivalent AML/CFT requirements to those of the EU. This equivalence determination allows for adjusted group-level compliance obligations for subsidiaries in those third countries.

The Commission shall assess the money-laundering, terrorist-financing and sanctions-evasion risks affecting the internal market and cross-border activities. The report is due by 10 July 2028 and is updated every four years thereafter. It identifies cross-border risks and sectoral vulnerabilities; obliged entities must take it into account in their business-wide risk assessment under AMLR Art. 10.

metadata.source_quote: Directive (EU) 2024/1640 Art. 7: "The Commission shall conduct an assessment of the risks of money laundering and terrorist financing and of non-implementation and evasion of targeted financial sanctions affecting the internal market and relating to cross-border activities."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amld6-2024.txt

description: Member States may conduct ad hoc sectoral risk assessments in addition to the national risk assessment, where the risk situation so requires. The Commission may recommend that a Member State carry one out. Sectoral findings inform the risk factors obliged entities must reflect in their own risk assessments.

metadata.source_quote: Directive (EU) 2024/1640 Art. 8: "Where Member States consider that the risk situation so requires, they may review the national risk assessment more frequently or conduct ad hoc sectoral risk assessments."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amld6-2024.txt

description: The management body of an obliged entity bears ultimate responsibility for AML/CFT compliance. At least one member must have adequate knowledge of AML/CFT risks. The management body approves the BWRA, internal policies, and compliance programme.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 12: management body SHALL bear responsibility

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 13 — Risk Variables and Factors
description: Sets out the risk variables and factors obliged entities must consider in their risk assessments, including customer, product/service, geographic, and delivery channel factors. References Annexes II and III. AMLA shall develop RTS specifying minimum risk assessment requirements.

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 9 — Internal Policies, Procedures and Controls
description: Obliged entities must establish and maintain policies, controls, and procedures to mitigate ML/TF risks identified in their BWRA. The nature and extent of controls must be proportionate to identified risks, and must be reviewed regularly.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 9: "The policies, procedures and controls referred to in the first subparagraph shall be proportionate to the nature of the business, including its risks and complexity, and the size of the obliged entity and shall cover all the activities of the obliged entity that fall under the scope of this Regulation. 2."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.14 to Art.9 by reading the article; quote verbatim

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 17 — Branches and Subsidiaries in Third Countries
description: Where group subsidiaries or branches are established in third countries with less stringent AML/CFT requirements, the group parent must ensure those entities apply EU-standard measures to the extent permitted by local law. Impediments must be notified to the home Member State supervisor.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 17: "Where branches or subsidiaries of obliged entities are located in third countries where the minimum AML/CFT requirements are less strict than those set out in this Regulation, the parent undertaking shall ensure that those branches or subsidiaries comply with the requirements laid down in this Regulation, including requirements concerning data protection, or equivalent. 2."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.16 to Art.17 against the Official Journal text; quote verbatim

description: Obliged entities must screen employees involved in AML/CFT compliance functions for integrity and competence. Includes pre-employment background checks and ongoing assessment. Ensures staff in sensitive positions are not themselves involved in criminal activity.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 13: "The intensity of the subsequent assessments shall be determined on the basis of the tasks entrusted to the person and risks associated with the function they perform. 2."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.19 to Art.13 by reading the article; quote verbatim

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 22 — Identification of Beneficial Owners
description: Obliged entities must identify and verify the beneficial owner(s) of legal entities and legal arrangements as part of CDD. For companies: 25% or more ownership or control threshold identifies the beneficial owner. Where no natural person is identified at that threshold, the senior managing officials must be identified as the (substitute) BO. For trusts and similar arrangements: no percentage threshold applies — settlor, all trustees, protector, all beneficiaries, and any natural person exercising effective control must be identified.

metadata.threshold_note: 25% threshold for companies; no threshold for trusts/legal arrangements
metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 22: obliged entities SHALL identify and verify the identity of beneficial owners

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 22 — Identification and Verification of Customers and Beneficial Owners
description: Sets out the measures obliged entities must take to verify BO identity, including consulting national BO registers, collecting documents, and applying risk-based independent verification. Where BO cannot be verified, the business relationship must not be established or continued.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 22: "For the purposes of identifying the beneficial owner of a legal entity or of a legal arrangement, obliged entities shall collect the information referred to in Article 62(1), second subparagraph, point (a)."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.23 to Art.22 by reading the article; quote verbatim

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 58 — Beneficial Owners of Express Trusts
description: Specific CDD requirements for customers that are express trusts or similar legal arrangements. Trustees must identify themselves as trustees. All natural persons in the trust structure — settlor, trustees, protector, beneficiaries, and persons exercising effective control — must be identified and verified.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 58: "The beneficial owners of express trusts shall be all the following natural persons: (a) the settlors;"
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.24 to Art.58 against the Official Journal text; quote verbatim

description: CDD must generally be completed before establishing a business relationship or executing a transaction. In limited circumstances and for lower-risk situations, verification of identity may be completed during the course of establishing the relationship, provided transactions are restricted until CDD is complete.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 23: "Verification of the identity of the customer, the beneficial owner, and of any persons pursuant to Article 20(1), points (h) and (i), shall take place before the establishment of a business relationship or the carrying out of an occasional transaction."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.26 to Art.23 by reading the article; quote verbatim

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 26 — Ongoing Monitoring of the Business Relationship
description: Obliged entities must apply CDD measures to existing customers at appropriate intervals, in particular when customer circumstances change. Risk-based approach governs the timing and frequency of periodic reviews. Higher-risk customers require more frequent reassessment.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 26: "In the context of the ongoing monitoring referred to in paragraph 1, obliged entities shall ensure that the relevant documents, data or information of the customer are kept up to date."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.27 to Art.26 by reading the article; quote verbatim

description: Where obliged entities appoint agents or distributors to perform CDD on their behalf, ultimate responsibility for compliance failures remains with the principal entity. Clear contractual arrangements, training, and oversight of agents are required.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 18: "The obliged entity shall remain fully liable for any action, whether an act of commission or omission, connected to the outsourced tasks that are carried out by service providers."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 23 — Account Opening Before Verification (Financial Sector)
description: Financial sector-specific rules allow credit and financial institutions to open accounts before identity verification is complete, provided that transactions are restricted until verification is finalized. Applicable only where ML/TF risk is assessed as low and strict conditions are met.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 23: "By way of derogation from paragraph 1 of this Article, a credit institution or financial institution may open an account, including accounts that permit transactions in transferable securities, as may be required by a customer provided that there are adequate safeguards in place to ensure that transactions are not carried out by the customer or on its behalf until full compliance with the customer due diligence measures laid down in Article 20(1), points (a) and (b), is obtained."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 33 — Simplified Due Diligence Measures
description: Specifies the conditions under which simplified due diligence measures may be applied: the customer or product must exhibit low-risk characteristics as listed in Annex I, no ML/TF suspicion may exist, and the customer must not be a PEP or from a high-risk third country.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 33: "However, obliged entities shall carry out sufficient monitoring of the transactions and business relationship to enable the detection of unusual or suspicious transactions. 2."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.32 to Art.33 by reading the article; quote verbatim

description: Lists the customer, product/service, geographic, and delivery channel factors that indicate lower ML/TF risk for SDD eligibility. References Annex I. Includes regulated financial institutions, listed companies, government/public bodies, low-value insurance products, and basic payment accounts.

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 34 — Scope of Application of Enhanced Due Diligence
description: Specifies circumstances requiring enhanced due diligence beyond standard CDD: customers from high-risk third countries, PEPs, complex/large/unusual transactions with no apparent economic purpose, business relationships with non-face-to-face elements in higher-risk contexts.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 34: "In the cases referred to in Articles 29, 30, 31 and 36 to 46, as well as in other cases of higher risk that are identified by obliged entities pursuant to Article 20(2), second subparagraph, obliged entities shall apply enhanced due diligence measures to manage and mitigate such risks appropriately. 2."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.35 to Art.34 by reading the article; quote verbatim

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 36 — EDD for High-Risk Third Countries
description: Mandatory EDD for business relationships or transactions involving natural or legal persons from EU-designated high-risk third countries. Measures include: enhanced monitoring, senior management approval, verification of source of funds and source of wealth, and additional document collection.

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 34 — Enhanced Due Diligence Measures
description: Details the specific additional measures in EDD situations: obtaining additional information on the customer, BO, and source of wealth/funds; obtaining senior management approval before establishing or continuing the relationship; enhanced and more frequent monitoring of transactions.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 34: "With the exception of the cases covered by Section 2 of this Chapter, in cases of higher risk as referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, obliged entities shall apply enhanced due diligence measures, proportionate to the higher risks identified, which may include the following measures:"
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 39 — Nominee Shareholders and Directors
description: Where nominee shareholders or directors are used, obliged entities must identify both the nominee and the person on whose behalf they act (the underlying principal). Nominee arrangements cannot be used to obscure beneficial ownership.

Obliged entities must apply specific risk-mitigating measures for non-face-to-face customer onboarding and business relationships. Technology-based identification and verification methods (eIDAS-compliant electronic ID, video identification, biometric checks) may be used where appropriately risk-assessed. The use of remote identification must be documented in the BWRA and subject to appropriate controls.

metadata.obligation_type_note: Art. 40: specific controls required for non-face-to-face relationships

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 10 — New Products and Technologies Risk Assessment
description: Obliged entities must identify and assess ML/TF risks arising from new products, business practices, delivery mechanisms, and technologies before launch, including anonymity-enhancing tools. AMLA may issue guidance on emerging technology risks.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 10: "Prior to the launch of new products, services or business practices, including the use of new delivery channels and new or developing technologies, in conjunction with new or pre-existing products and services or before starting to provide an existing service or product to a new customer segment or in a new geographical area, obliged entities shall identify and assess, in particular, the related money laundering and terrorist financing risks and take appropriate measures to manage and mitigate those risks."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 39 — Prohibition on Correspondent Relationships with Shell Institutions
description: Credit institutions are prohibited from entering into or continuing correspondent banking relationships with shell banks. Obliged entities must not engage in relationships with financial institutions that permit their accounts to be used by shell banks.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 39: "Credit institutions and financial institutions shall not enter into, or continue, a correspondent relationship with a shell institution."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.42 to Art.39 against the Official Journal text; quote verbatim

description: AMLA shall establish and maintain a publicly accessible list of the specific functions in each Member State and international organisations that qualify as prominent public functions for PEP classification purposes. Member States must notify AMLA of qualifying functions.

Persons who have ceased to hold a prominent public function remain subject to enhanced measures for an appropriate risk-based period, determined by factors including the nature of the function and residual risk. AMLR mandates no fixed cessation period — the assessment must be risk-sensitive.

metadata.note: No fixed cessation period — risk-based assessment required per Art. 45(4)

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 46 — Senior Management Approval for PEPs
description: Obliged entities must obtain senior management approval before establishing or continuing a business relationship with a PEP. The level of seniority required for approval must be proportionate to the risk posed by the specific PEP.

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 46 — PEP Family Members and Close Associates
description: Enhanced scrutiny must be applied to family members (spouse/partner, children and their partners, parents) and known close associates of PEPs. Obliged entities must take reasonable steps to identify PEP relationships at onboarding and on an ongoing basis.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 46: "The measures referred to in Articles 42, 44 and 45 shall also apply to family members or persons known to be close associates of politically exposed persons."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.47 to Art.46 against the Official Journal text; quote verbatim

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 44 — PEPs as Insurance Policy Beneficiaries
description: Life insurance and investment-related insurance undertakings must check whether policy beneficiaries and their beneficial owners are PEPs. A PEP beneficiary triggers senior management notification and enhanced scrutiny at payout or assignment of the policy.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 44: "Obliged entities shall take reasonable measures to determine whether the beneficiaries of a life or other investment-related insurance policy or, where relevant, the beneficial owner of the beneficiary are politically exposed persons."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — reference corrected from Art.48 to Art.44 against the Official Journal text; quote verbatim

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 49 — Targeted Financial Sanctions Screening
description: Obliged entities must screen customers, beneficial owners, and transaction counterparties against EU, UN, and applicable national targeted financial sanctions lists. Screening must occur before establishing business relationships, before executing transactions, and on an ongoing basis when lists are updated.

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 50 — Internal Reporting to MLRO
description: Employees who know or suspect that a transaction or activity involves ML/TF must report through internal channels to the MLRO. Obliged entities must establish clear, secure internal reporting procedures and protect employees who report from retaliation.

Obliged entities and their employees must not disclose to the customer or any third party that a SAR has been filed, that an investigation is underway, or that information has been requested by authorities. Violation is a criminal offence under AMLD6.

Obliged entities and their employees who report suspicions to FIUs in good faith are protected from civil, criminal, administrative, and professional liability, even if the suspicion proves unfounded. Member States must ensure effective legal and employment protection against retaliation.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 72: "Disclosure of information to the FIU in good faith by an obliged entity or by an employee or director of such an obliged entity in accordance with Articles 69 and 70 shall not constitute a breach of any restriction on disclosure of information imposed by contract or by any legislative, regulatory or administrative provision, and shall not involve the obliged entity or its directors or employees in liability of any kind even in circumstances where they were not precisely aware of the underlying criminal activity and regardless of whether illegal activity actually occurred."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

canonical_name: AMLR Art. 69 — Provision of Information to the FIU
description: Obliged entities must promptly provide additional information to FIUs upon request, following SAR filing or as part of ongoing investigations. Must grant access to records and documentation within the scope of the request.

metadata.source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 69: "Obliged entities, and, where applicable, their directors and employees, shall cooperate fully with the FIU by promptly: (a) reporting to the FIU, on their own initiative, where the obliged entity knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect that funds or activities, regardless of the amount involved, are the proceeds of criminal activity or are related to terrorist financing or criminal activity and by responding to requests by the FIU for additional information in such cases; (b) providing the FIU, at its request, with all necessary information, including information on transaction records, within the deadlines imposed."
metadata.source_verified: 2026-08-29 — extracted verbatim from data/sources/amlr-2024-1624.txt

description: Formal written assessment of ML/TF risks across all products, services, customers, delivery channels, and geographies. Required at least annually and upon material changes. Must be approved by the management body and available to supervisors on request.

Structured process for identifying and verifying customer identity, understanding the purpose and nature of the business relationship, identifying beneficial owners, and assessing customer ML/TF risk. Foundation of the AML/CFT compliance programme.

Intensified CDD measures for higher-risk customers and situations: additional information collection, source of funds/wealth verification, senior management approval, and enhanced transaction monitoring. Mandatory for HRTCs, PEPs, and complex/unusual transactions.

Reduced CDD measures for verified low-risk situations as documented in the entity's BWRA. The degree of simplification must be proportionate and documented. Cannot apply where ML/TF suspicion exists, to PEPs, or to HRTC customers.

Systematic review of customer transactions to detect patterns inconsistent with the customer's known profile, risk rating, and expected business activity. Combines automated rule-based alerts and scenario detection with human review and escalation workflows.

End-to-end process for identifying, triaging, and reporting ML/TF suspicions to the national FIU. Stages: detection/alert, internal triage, MLRO investigation, decision, SAR completion and filing, record retention, and FIU cooperation on follow-up requests.

Process for identifying and verifying the natural persons who ultimately own or control a customer legal entity or arrangement. Includes BO declarations, consulting national BO registers, and independent document-based verification proportionate to risk.

Systematic screening of customers, beneficial owners, and transaction parties against PEP lists and commercial databases. Applied at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Must capture family members (Art. 47) and close associates. Positive matches require EDD and senior management approval.

Screening of customers, beneficial owners, and counterparties against EU/UN/national targeted financial sanctions lists. Applied before establishing relationships, before transactions, and when sanctions lists are updated. Positive matches trigger asset freeze and competent authority notification.

Continuous monitoring throughout the lifecycle of the business relationship: periodic CDD refresh, risk re-rating when circumstances change, transaction pattern analysis, and updating CDD documentation. Frequency must be risk-based.

Systematic retention of CDD documents, transaction records, SAR correspondence, and monitoring results for the required periods (5 years from end of relationship/transaction, extendable to 10 years by national law). Records must be retrievable and provided to supervisors on request.

The overarching process of calibrating AML/CFT controls to identified risk levels. Encompasses BWRA, customer risk scoring, product/service risk assessment, and proportionate control design. The foundational principle of AMLR and FATF standards.

EU supervisory authority established by Regulation (EU) 2024/1620, headquartered in Frankfurt. Operational from 1 July 2025. Will directly supervise selected high-risk credit institutions and CASPs from January 2028. Issues binding RTS/ITS and guidelines for the EU AML/CFT framework.

The European Commission designates high-risk third countries (delegated regulations), publishes the biennial SNRA, adopts delegated and implementing acts under AMLR (including the HRTC list), and proposes amendments to the AML/CFT legislative framework.
Secure platform hosted at Europol facilitating cross-border exchange of financial intelligence between EU national FIUs. Enables joint analysis and coordinated response to cross-border ML/TF threats.

National authorities in each Member State responsible for supervising obliged entities' compliance with AMLR and national AML/CFT law. Typically financial supervisors, central banks, or dedicated AML units. Will continue supervising most entities after AMLA begins direct supervision of highest-risk entities.

International standard-setter for AML/CFT and CPF, comprising 37 member jurisdictions. AMLR implements FATF's 40 Recommendations and 11 Immediate Outcomes. FATF mutual evaluation findings influence EU supervisory priorities and HRTC designations.

From 2020-2025, EBA held EU-level AML/CFT supervisory convergence responsibilities including issuing binding RTS, conducting peer reviews, and maintaining the AML/CFT college network. These responsibilities transferred to AMLA upon its establishment in July 2025.

canonical_name: AMLA RTS on Customer Risk Variables (Art. 13)
description: AMLA RTS specifying the minimum requirements for customer risk assessments: mandatory risk variables, risk factors, and risk scoring methodology. Mandated by AMLR Art. 13. Status: consultation phase (AMLA work programme 2025-2026).

RTS specifying the content, format, and minimum requirements for group-level AML/CFT policies, including requirements for ensuring policy compliance in third-country subsidiaries and handling of legal impediments.

canonical_name: AMLA RTS on CDD Information Requirements
description: RTS specifying the minimum information to be collected and verified as part of standard CDD, EDD, and SDD. Covers identification documents, verification methods, and BO information requirements across different customer categories.

canonical_name: AMLA RTS on Remote Customer Identification
description: RTS specifying technical requirements and security standards for non-face-to-face customer identification and verification, including digital identity, video verification, and electronic signatures.

canonical_name: AMLA RTS on EDD Measures for HRTCs (Art. 36)
description: RTS specifying the minimum EDD measures obliged entities must apply when dealing with customers or transactions from Commission-designated high-risk third countries.

canonical_name: AMLA RTS on Beneficial Ownership Register Standards
description: RTS governing technical standards for the interconnection of national BO registers, including data format, API standards, and cross-border access rules for the central EU BO register portal.

ITS specifying the format, templates, and data standards for supervisory reporting by obliged entities to competent authorities, and by competent authorities to AMLA for the purposes of regulatory oversight.

canonical_name: AMLA RTS on Data Points for Reporting
description: RTS specifying the data points that obliged entities must maintain for AML/CFT compliance purposes and be able to report to supervisors and AMLA on request, including CDD data elements, transaction records, and SAR statistics.

The risk that an obliged entity's products, services, customers, or channels are used to launder criminal proceeds. Encompasses the three classic stages: placement (introducing funds), layering (concealment), and integration (reintroducing clean funds).

The risk that funds are raised or moved through an obliged entity to support terrorist activities. Distinct from ML risk: TF may involve small amounts and legitimate sources of funds, requiring different detection approaches.

The risk that funds or financial services are used to support the financing of weapons of mass destruction proliferation in violation of UN Security Council resolutions. Required to be addressed through targeted financial sanctions screening under AMLR Art. 49.

The risk that customers or transactions are used to circumvent EU, UN, or national targeted financial sanctions programmes. Obliged entities must maintain dedicated sanctions screening controls and escalation procedures.

FATF's public listing of jurisdictions under increased monitoring due to strategic AML/CFT deficiencies that they have committed to addressing. Greylisted jurisdictions are candidates for EU HRTC designation, triggering mandatory EDD obligations for obliged entities.

FATF's listing of jurisdictions with serious, unaddressed AML/CFT deficiencies that pose a significant threat to the international financial system. Typically triggers mandatory EU HRTC designation with the most severe countermeasures.

Criminal activities whose proceeds can give rise to ML. AMLR and 6AMLD adopt an all-crimes approach — all serious criminal offences including tax crimes, corruption, fraud, drug trafficking, human trafficking, and cybercrime are predicate offences.

The fundamental principle that AML/CFT measures should be proportionate to the ML/TF risks identified. Higher-risk situations require more intensive controls; lower-risk situations allow proportionately lighter measures. Core to both FATF Recommendation 1 and AMLR Art. 8.

AMLD6 establishes the supervisory framework complementing AMLR: designation of national competent authorities, supervisory colleges, cooperation with AMLA, and supervisory convergence obligations. Governance of AML supervision sits in AMLD6 rather than AMLR.

AMLD6 requires Member States to establish criminal sanctions for ML offences including: effective, proportionate, and dissuasive penalties for natural and legal persons; minimum standards for tipping-off and obstruction offences; and rules on corporate liability.

AMLD6 governs FIU establishment, operational independence, powers to obtain and use financial intelligence, feedback obligations to reporting entities, and cross-border cooperation through FIU.net and joint analysis teams.

AMLD6 requires Member States to maintain central beneficial ownership registers for legal entities and legal arrangements, specifying access conditions (competent authorities, obliged entities, public access), data quality standards, and interconnection via BRIS.

Member States must transpose AMLD6 into national law by 10 July 2026, one year before AMLR application date. Coordinated transposition is critical to ensure the supervisory and criminal law framework is in place when AMLR obligations apply.

The Fourth Anti-Money Laundering Directive, whose customer-facing provisions (CDD, BO, reporting) are largely superseded by AMLR. Supervisory and institutional provisions are superseded by AMLD6. 4AMLD remains in force until AMLR and AMLD6 apply.

Extends FATF Recommendation 16 travel rule to crypto-asset transfers. PSPs must accompany wire transfers with full payer/payee data (€1,000 threshold for non-PSP transfers). CASPs must include full originator/beneficiary info for ALL crypto transfers with NO minimum threshold.

AML/CFT data processing requires a lawful basis under GDPR Art. 6. The primary basis is Art. 6(1)(c) — processing necessary for compliance with a legal obligation (AMLR). Stub entity — enriched with full article detail in the GDPR/AI Act knowledge pack.

DORA Art. 9 requires financial entities to implement ICT security policies. AML transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and SAR filing systems are financial entity ICT systems subject to DORA operational resilience requirements. Enriched in DORA/NIS2 pack.

CASPs authorised under MiCA automatically become obliged entities under AMLR. The MiCA authorisation process and the AML supervisory regime are coordinated via AMLA and national supervisors. Enriched in Banking Prudential pack.

canonical_name: AMLR Annex I — Potentially Low-Risk Factors
description: Lists customer, product/service, geographic, and delivery channel factors that may indicate lower ML/TF risk and support application of simplified due diligence. Referenced by Art. 33. Factors include: regulated financial institutions, listed companies, public authorities, low-value insurance products, and certain financial products.

canonical_name: AMLR Annex II — Potentially High-Risk Factors
description: Lists customer, product/service, geographic, and delivery channel factors that may indicate higher ML/TF risk and trigger enhanced due diligence. Referenced by Art. 13. Factors include: cash-intensive businesses, PEP-related relationships, HRTCs, non-face-to-face relationships, and complex ownership structures.
